title: Your first agent in the terminal
brief: Build the first working version of minidsh: a terminal program that answers questions by letting a DeepSeek model read files in the current folder. You write the model call, one tool described by a schema, the loop that runs the model's tool calls and sends back their results, a cap on steps per turn, and error results for every way a tool call can fail. When you finish, `npx tsx src/cli.ts "What does the file named in index.txt say?"` prints the right answer after reading two files, and a misspelled file name produces a helpful answer instead of a crash.

starter.note: Contains `"type": "module"` so top-level await works; no dependencies are needed, tsx runs through npx.
Message, ToolCall, ToolSchema and Tool, exactly as the lessons define them.

complete(messages, schemas) calls https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions with model deepseek-flash and thinking: { type: 'disabled' } (with tools, thinking mode would require sending reasoning_content back) and returns { message, finish }; toWire converts your messages to the wire format.
readFileSchema, readFileTool and runCall, which turns every failure into an `Error:` result.
runTurn(history, userText, tools, maxSteps = 8): the agent loop with a step limit.
Runs one turn for a question given on the command line, or a chat when none is given.
A test file containing only the text notes.txt.
A test file containing: Buy milk. Call Sam.

hints: Export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in your shell before running anything; a 401 status means the key is missing or wrong.
Print `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)` once from complete to see the exact shape of a reply with tool_calls before you write the conversion.
`function.arguments` is a string of JSON, not an object; keep it raw in ToolCall and parse it only in runCall.
Push the assistant message that holds the tool calls into the history before you push any tool results, and give every call id exactly one result.
Send progress lines such as `[step 1/8] read_file {...}` to console.error so the answer on standard output stays clean.
To test the step limit without spending many tokens, call runTurn with maxSteps = 1 on the index.txt question; it needs 3 steps, so it must stop and say so.

rubric.criterion: complete() sends the request with the API key from the environment and reads choices[0].message and usage from the JSON reply
The history keeps system, user, assistant and tool messages in order and is resent in full on every request
complete() returns the finish reason, and a cut-off (length) reply is never shown as a complete answer
read_file is described with a name, a description that tells the model what it returns, and a JSON Schema with a required path
Tool calls from the reply are converted into ToolCall objects with id, name and raw JSON arguments
Each tool call gets exactly one tool message carrying its call id, placed after the assistant message that requested it
runTurn repeats model request, tool runs and results until a reply has no tool calls
Each line the user enters starts a new turn on the same history, and steps are numbered in the progress output
A turn that reaches maxSteps ends with a clear note to the user and a valid history
Unknown tool names, invalid JSON arguments and thrown exceptions each become an Error: result for that call id instead of a crash

milestones.title: Ask the model one question
milestones.body: Write src/types.ts with Message and src/llm.ts with complete(messages). Make src/cli.ts send the command-line argument as a user message after a short system prompt, and print the reply text and the finish reason.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx src/cli.ts "What is the capital of France?"

milestones.title: Offer read_file and catch its tool call
milestones.body: Add ToolSchema and ToolCall to src/types.ts, readFileSchema to src/tools.ts, and send it in the request's tools list. Convert any tool_calls in the reply into ToolCall objects and print them. Nothing runs yet; you should see one call to read_file with the path notes.txt and finish reason tool_calls.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx src/cli.ts "What does notes.txt say?"

milestones.title: Run the loop to a final answer
milestones.body: Add the tool role and toolCallId, toWire, readFileTool and runTurn in src/loop.ts. The loop runs every tool call, adds each result with its call id, and repeats until the reply is plain text. The index.txt question should print two [step n] lines on standard error and an answer that mentions buying milk and calling Sam.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx src/cli.ts "What does the file named in index.txt say?"

milestones.title: Cap the steps in a turn
milestones.body: Give runTurn a maxSteps parameter, default 8, and read an optional MAX_STEPS environment variable in src/cli.ts. When the cap is reached, push and return a note such as "Stopped after 1 steps without a final answer." With MAX_STEPS=1 the index.txt question must stop with that note instead of answering.
milestones.checkCmd: MAX_STEPS=1 npx tsx src/cli.ts "What does the file named in index.txt say?"

milestones.title: Turn failures into error results
milestones.body: Add runCall to src/tools.ts and use it in runTurn, so an unknown tool name, invalid JSON arguments and a thrown exception each become an Error: result for that call id. Ask about a file that does not exist: the program must not crash, and the model's answer should say it could not find the file or name the file it found instead.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx src/cli.ts "What does note.txt say?"
